newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-DOMINICAN REPUBLIC WINS CARIBBEAN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DOMINICAN REPUBLIC WINS CARIBBEAN SERIES.

text.p: The Dominican Republic's Cibao Eagles claimed the Caribbean Series baseball championship on Sunday by winning their fourth straight game, defeating Mexico's Culiacan Tomato Growers 4-3.

The Dominicans outnumbered Mexico in major league players 12 to one, but Mexico pulled within one run of them in the eighth inning when designated hitter Matt Stark launched a towering two-run homer into the left-field seats off the first pitch from star Dominican reliever Dario Veras to make it 4-3.
That set off a wild celebration from the Mexican fans who packed the 15,500-seat Hector Espino Stadium in the Sonora desert 165 miles (265 km) south of the U.S. border.
But Veras set Mexico down in the top of the ninth to save the game for the Dominican Republic.
The Dominican team lost the first two games of the six-day round-robin tournament, but came roaring back with a lineup full of hot bats to deny Mexico its second straight Caribbean Series title.
The series features the professional winter league champions of the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Venezuela and Puerto Rico.
Tony Bautista, a second baseman who also plays with Major League Baseball's Oakland A's, belted a three-run homer in the bottom of the first inning to give the Dominican Republic an early lead.
The homer ended the hot streak of Mexican starting pitcher Martin Hernandez, who was 5-0 in the playoffs of the Mexican Pacific League and won his opening start against Venezuela.
Bautista, the cleanup hitter, finished the six-game series with a .384 average, two homers and a series-leading 13 RBIs.

Dominican Republic manager Mike Quade used a committee of pitchers, led by starter Jose Parra of the Minnesota Twins, who shut Mexico down on one hit and four walks while striking out four over four innings.
Dominican catcher Guillermo Garcia, who had three homers and eight RBIs in the series, drove in the other Dominican run with a sacrifice fly to right in the sixth inning.

Down 4-0, Mexico mounted a threat in the top of the seventh when it scored a run on Darryl Brinkley's RBI single to put runners at the corners. But on the next play, Adan Amezcua, the runner at third base, was thrown out at the plate on an infield grounder.
Brinkley later was the third out in the inning when, from third base, he tried an ill-advised steal of home and got caught in a rundown.
Venezuela's Magellan Navigators overcame a seven-run deficit to defeat Puerto Rico's Mayaguez Indians 11-9 in the earlier game.

The two teams were playing for little more than pride as both had been eliminated from winning the championship Saturday. Venezuela finished with a 3-3 record and Puerto Rico, the team with the most major leaguers (13), went home in last place with a 2-4 record after starting out 2-0.

Venezuela exploded for five runs in the bottom of the eighth, one on a home run by Eddy Diaz, two on a game-tying double by Luis Solo and two more on a double by cleanup hitter Luis Raven to give Venezuela its 11-9 margin.
Venezuelan closer Oscar Henriquez held the previously hot Puerto Rican bats silent in the top of the ninth to earn the save.

Puerto Rico had jumped to a 9-2 lead in the third, largely behind leadoff hitter Armando Rios, who homered in the first and second innings and doubled in the third, scoring three times and driving in five. Rios finished with four home runs in the six-game series.
Edward Guzman also homered for Puerto Rico, which got 10 of its 12 hits in the first three innings.

But three Venezuelan relievers then shut down Puerto Rico, and Venezuela got back into the game with four runs in the sixth to make the score 9-6. Three of those runs came on a homer by designated hitter Any Freire.
Sojo, a shortstop who also plays as a utility infielder for the New York Yankess, went 3-for-3 with three RBI to finish the six-game series with a .478 average, one home run and six RBI.
